title: In MLB the model stays less certain than the market for most of the game
headline_insight: On the segment-clean corpus the model carries MORE uncertainty than the market through innings 1 to 8 (0.976 against 0.9553 bits at inning 1) and only becomes the sharper of the two at inning 9 (0.4181 against 0.4589); their disagreement runs 0.0839 early to 0.2067 late.
what_it_means: This outcome-free view tracks two things over game time: how far apart the forecasters sit (gap) and how much uncertainty each still carries (entropy, in bits). On the segment-clean MLB corpus the market resolves uncertainty faster than the model for eight of the ten innings, and the two only cross at inning 9. In soccer they converge instead (gap shrinks by -0.0732) as entropy decays toward zero.
how_to_read: Higher entropy means more uncertainty (1.0 bit at a coin-flip, 0.0 at a certainty); watch whether the model line drops below the market line as the game runs.
why_it_matters: It says where each forecaster commits. Revision 1 showed the model growing certain far ahead of the market, which read as unearned late-game confidence; on the segment-clean corpus that reverses for most of the game and only the ninth inning still shows the model ahead.
caveat: This is a labeled STANDARD_INSTRUMENT with no outcomes attached; entropy decay late in a game is expected, so it describes behavior rather than scoring accuracy. The inning-10 checkpoint rests on 46 ticks, just above the 30-row floor, so read the last point as thin.
